import numpy as np

# Data for Jan-Mar 1940 (in thousands of dollars)
months = np.array([1, 2, 3])  # January, February, March

# Individual and Corporation collections (in thousands)
individual = np.array([20561, 43443, 356076])
corporation = np.array([25128, 27503, 298548])

# Calculate ratios (Individual / Corporation)
ratios = individual / corporation

print("Ratios for each month:")
print(f"January (x=1): {ratios[0]}")
print(f"February (x=2): {ratios[1]}")
print(f"March (x=3): {ratios[2]}")

# Linear regression: y = mx + b
# Using numpy polyfit (degree 1)
slope, intercept = np.polyfit(months, ratios, 1)

print(f"\nLinear Regression Results:")
print(f"Slope: {slope}")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept}")
print(f"\nSlope rounded to thousandths: {round(slope, 3)}")

# Data for Jan-Mar 1940 (in thousands of dollars)
months = [1, 2, 3]  # January, February, March

# Individual and Corporation collections (in thousands)
individual = [20561, 43443, 356076]
corporation = [25128, 27503, 298548]

# Calculate ratios (Individual / Corporation)
ratios = [individual[i] / corporation[i] for i in range(3)]

print("Ratios for each month:")
print(f"January (x=1): {ratios[0]}")
print(f"February (x=2): {ratios[1]}")
print(f"March (x=3): {ratios[2]}")

# Linear regression: y = mx + b
# Calculate slope using least squares formula
n = len(months)
x_mean = sum(months) / n
y_mean = sum(ratios) / n

# Calculate slope
numerator = sum((months[i] - x_mean) * (ratios[i] - y_mean) for i in range(n))
denominator = sum((months[i] - x_mean) ** 2 for i in range(n))
slope = numerator / denominator

# Calculate intercept
intercept = y_mean - slope * x_mean

print(f"\nLinear Regression Results:")
print(f"Slope: {slope}")
print(f"Intercept: {intercept}")
print(f"\nSlope rounded to thousandths: {round(slope, 3)}")
EOF
